findings.title: Closing the modal on the backup codes step via backdrop or Escape key leaves 2FA UI state stale and modal state unreset
findings.body: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, enabling 2FA now transitions to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` and defers calling `onEnable()` and `resetState()` until the user clicks the "Close" button (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`). However, `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>` still allows the user to dismiss the dialog by clicking the backdrop, pressing Escape, or clicking the dialog's close icon, which triggers `onOpenChange` directly without calling `onEnable()` or `resetState()`. Because the backend has already enabled 2FA at that point, dismissing the dialog that way leaves the parent settings page showing 2FA as disabled and leaves `step` stuck on `DisplayBackupCodes` if the modal is reopened.

findings.title: Third-party IdP users with 2FA enabled cannot log in or use backup codes
findings.body: In `next-auth-options.ts` (lines 114-129), the checks for third-party identity providers (`user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL`) and password verification only skip execution when `credentials.totpCode` is truthy (`!credentials.totpCode`), without checking `credentials.backupCode`. Furthermore, in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` (lines 180-183), when `totpEmail` is set (the JWT-based 2FA flow used for Google/SAML logins), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, so the "Lost access" button to switch to a backup code is never shown, and even if a backup code were submitted, `authorize` would reject it with `ThirdPartyIdentityProviderEnabled` because `credentials.totpCode` is empty.

findings.title: First 2FA E2E test does not complete the new backup codes step and passes due to a broken assertion
findings.body: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the first test (`"should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA"`) was not updated to close the new backup codes modal step (`backup-codes-close`) after `fillOtp`. As noted by the `FIXME` comment added on line 50, `expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` passes only because `isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>` (which is always truthy when not `await`ed and without `.resolves`), while the modal is still open over the page and `onEnable()` has never been called.
